# sonrai_organization_policy (Resource)

Defines an organization policy: a service control policy or resource control policy of your own that the firewall deploys alongside its own. AWS only.

Sonrai does not create a separate policy in AWS. When the policy is deployed its statements are packed into the policies Sonrai already manages at each scope, so it uses none of the scope's policy attachment slots.

Defining a policy takes effect in Sonrai as soon as it is applied, and on its own it is in force nowhere. Attach it with `sonrai_organization_policy_attachment`; that part is staged and submitted like any other control.

The platform does not keep policy names unique. A managed policy that already has this name -- made in the console, or by another configuration -- is rejected rather than adopted; import it instead.

~> **Editing a policy that is deployed needs a redeploy.** The definition changes at once, but everywhere it is deployed keeps enforcing the old document until its root scope is submitted and deployed again. Reference `revision` in the `triggers` of each `sonrai_control_submission` and that happens in the same apply. The apply warns with the root scopes affected, which can include ones this configuration does not manage. Until it is deployed, the edit can be reverted from Pending Changes in the console, which the next plan reports as drift.

~> **A policy that is attached cannot be destroyed in the same apply that detaches it.** The platform will not delete a policy that is still deployed, and detaching one only takes effect once that change is submitted and deployed. Remove the attachments and apply, then remove this resource and apply again. A plan that would destroy or replace a deployed policy is rejected, naming where it is deployed, before anything is changed. Attachments that were staged and never deployed are discarded with the policy.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A service control policy of your own. It is defined as soon as this is
# applied, and is in force nowhere until it is attached.
resource "sonrai_organization_policy" "deny_leaving_org" {
  root_scope  = "aws/r-abcd"
  name        = "deny-leaving-organization"
  policy_type = "SERVICE_CONTROL_POLICY"
  description = "Accounts cannot remove themselves from the organization"

  # The whole document. The plan has the platform check it.
  content = jsonencode({
    Version = "2012-10-17"
    Statement = [{
      Sid      = "DenyLeaveOrganization"
      Effect   = "Deny"
      Action   = ["organizations:LeaveOrganization"]
      Resource = "*"
    }]
  })
}

# Attaching is staged, and takes effect when submitted and deployed. The
# policy then applies to the organizational unit and everything beneath it.
resource "sonrai_organization_policy_attachment" "workloads" {
  policy_id   = sonrai_organization_policy.deny_leaving_org.id
  root_scope  = "aws/r-abcd"
  resource_id = "ou-abcd-1a2b3c4d"
}

resource "sonrai_control_submission" "firewall" {
  root_scope = "aws/r-abcd"

  triggers = {
    attachment = sonrai_organization_policy_attachment.workloads.revision
    # Moves when the deployed policy is edited, which is what redeploys it.
    # Without it the old document stays in force.
    policy = sonrai_organization_policy.deny_leaving_org.revision
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `content` (String) The policy document, as JSON. Use `jsonencode` or `data.aws_iam_policy_document`. This is the whole document: an edit replaces it. Formatting and key order are not significant. The plan has the platform check it, and fails with what it finds.
- `name` (String) Name of the policy. It can be changed in place. It cannot start with `Sonrai`, which the platform keeps for its own policies, and cannot begin or end with a space.
- `policy_type` (String) `SERVICE_CONTROL_POLICY` or `RESOURCE_CONTROL_POLICY`. Forces replacement. A resource control policy can only be deployed where the AWS organization has that policy type enabled.
- `root_scope` (String) Root scope of the AWS organization the policy is written for, for example `aws/r-abcd`. Forces replacement. The platform does not report it back, so it is taken from the configuration after an import.

### Optional

- `description` (String) What the policy is for. Once set it can be changed but not removed: the platform reads an empty description as "leave it as it is".

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Identifier the platform gave the policy. Give it to `sonrai_organization_policy_attachment` as `policy_id`.
- `revision` (String) Opaque value that changes when the policy needs redeploying: when a deployed policy is edited, and while such an edit is still waiting to be deployed. Reference it in the `triggers` of each `sonrai_control_submission` whose root scope the policy is attached under.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
# Import ID: the policy's id. Find it with the sonrai_organization_policies
# data source. Only a policy written in Sonrai can be imported, and content is
# the whole document, so write all of it or the next apply replaces the rest.
import {
  to = sonrai_organization_policy.deny_leaving_org
  id = "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import ID: the policy's id. Find it with the sonrai_organization_policies
# data source. Only a policy written in Sonrai can be imported.
terraform import sonrai_organization_policy.deny_leaving_org 'a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000'
```
